items.title: What Are Applied Materials Stock Investors Overlooking?
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) sold a record $7 billion of chipmaking tools in fiscal Q3 2026. That was about 77% of its $9.1 billion in revenue for the quarter. When you own the stock, you mostly own those tool sales. A record that large is easy to read as the new normal. So what might Applied Materials investors be overlooking about those tool sales.

items.title: Is KLA Stock Really Expensive?
items.summary: KLA's market value is 53.2 times its profit over the past twelve months, well above its three-year average of 36 times. A multiple that high means buyers are paying today for profit the company has not earned yet. So is KLA (KLAC) stock really expensive for the growth its business delivers.

items.title: Better Semiconductor Equipment Stock: Applied Materials vs. Lam Research
items.summary: The chipmaking equipment boom has supercharged growth for both companies, and their prospects suggest further upside in their stock prices.

items.title: Is Applied Materials Still The Business You Bought?
items.summary: You may own Applied Materials (AMAT) as a chip equipment maker that aims to hand most of its spare cash back to shareholders. A $10,000 holding a year ago is now worth about $24,500. Your stake in this business is far bigger than it was. Is Applied Materials still the business you bought.

items.title: Wall Street Bulls Look Optimistic About Lam Research (LRCX): Should You Buy?
items.summary: According to the average brokerage recommendation (ABR), one should invest in Lam Research (LRCX). It is debatable whether this highly sought-after metric is effective because Wall Street analysts' recommendations tend to be overly optimistic. Would it be worth investing in the stock?

items.title: Lam Research (LRCX) Following Higher 2026 Outlook And Packaging Growth Is It Still Undervalued
items.summary: Lam Research (LRCX) drew fresh attention after management lifted its 2026 wafer fab equipment outlook to the low US$150b range, while also flagging a sharp expected rise in advanced packaging revenue. Recent trading has been choppy for Lam Research, with the share price up 14.1% over the past week but down about 19% across the last three months.
